captive_summary: Cancelled pre-FEED concept from a BG Group/Petrobras/Repsol/Galp consortium exploring Santos Basin pre-salt FLNG export (ca. 2011-2013). Only substantive public record found is a 2011 report of Petrobras delaying the plan; no engineering/FEED study, vessel design, or power-system spec was ever published.
confirmed_how: Offshore Energy (5 Aug 2011) reported 'Brazil: Petrobras Delays FLNG Plan' for the Santos Basin project. No later FEED, contractor award, or design study surfaced via gem.wiki's own reference list or web search; GEM records the unit status as cancelled/confirmed with no vessel or capacity ever finalized. The only other indexed source (abarrelfull.wikidot.com) is a banned domain and was not consulted for content.
gogpt_prior_assessment: gogpt_prior = no. Nearest GOGPT plant is Euzébio Rocha power station (250 MW, 12.8 km) — an unrelated onshore/coastal plant with no documented project linkage to this cancelled offshore FLNG concept.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Project never reached FEED/design stage; no generating equipment was ever specified to exist, so there is nothing to add.
notes: Cancelled at concept stage; no vessel, sponsor design, or power system ever published beyond the 2011 delay report.

captive_summary: Sepetiba Bay FSRU (vessel 'LNGt Powership Asia') stores and regasifies LNG, piping gas onward to four Karpowership moored floating power plants (Karkey I & II, Porsud I & II) that together with the FSRU total 560 MW per Karpowership's own case study — but that is the PowerPlantsSupplied direction, not captive power to the terminal. No public source discloses the FSRU's own onboard generation equipment (make/model/fuel) distinct from the Powership fleet it feeds.
confirmed_how: Karpowership's Brazil case-study PDF states the Sepetiba complex 'has been operational in Sepetiba Bay, Brazil since 2022 and currently operates with 4 Powerships and 1 FSRU...generating 560 MW of electricity' — attributing the generation to the complex as a whole (the Powerships are the generating assets; GOGPT already tracks Porsud I at 116.2 MW and Porsud II at 78.3 MW as separate plants). Vessel-tracking/search for 'Powership Asia' / 'LNGt Powership Asia' technical specifications turned up AIS/registry pages only, no engine, generator, or fuel details for the FSRU itself.

verification_log.note: confirms complex-wide generation figure, not FSRU-specific

gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT neighbor Porsud I power station (116.2 MW, 0.11 km, operating) is one of Karpowership's own moored Powerships fed by this FSRU's regasified gas — a distinct power-generating vessel/facility owned by the same group, not the FSRU's own captive plant. Porsud II (78.3 MW) is its sister unit at the same site.
gogpt_candidate_basis: The FSRU may carry its own auxiliary/hotel-load generation (typical of modern FSRUs) but no source discloses it; Porsud I/II (and Karkey I/II) are already separately GOGPT-tracked as the actual generating plants fed by this terminal, so no new GOGPT record is indicated for the FSRU itself absent a disclosed nameplate.
notes: Clean direction-test case: Sepetiba Bay FSRU's entire commercial purpose is supplying regasified gas to Karpowership's 4 moored Powerships (Karkey I, Karkey II, Porsud I, Porsud II) for electricity generation — already correctly recorded in PowerPlantsSupplied, not a captive-power finding for this terminal.

hardware_summary: Wärtsilä dual-fuel diesel-electric (DFDE) generating plant aboard the FSRU vessel Energos Nanook (170,213 m³, ex-Golar Nanook, built 2018 by Samsung Heavy Industries), supplying the vessel's own electric load (regas/cargo systems, propulsion when underway) via gas/boil-off-fired gensets.
fuel_basis: Wärtsilä DFDE (Dual Fuel Diesel Electric) engines — the class-standard configuration runs primarily on boil-off/natural gas with liquid pilot fuel injection; documented on the vessel operator's (Energos Infrastructure) own fleet technical page.
captive_summary: The Sergipe FSRU's vessel, Energos Nanook, is fitted with Wärtsilä DFDE (dual-fuel diesel-electric) propulsion/generation per the vessel operator's own fleet spec page — a documented on-site gas-fired electric generating plant serving the vessel's own systems. This is separate from the 1,500 MW Porto de Sergipe combined-cycle power station the terminal supplies regasified gas to (PowerPlantsSupplied direction, already recorded in GEM).
confirmed_how: Energos Infrastructure's own fleet-assets page (energosinfra.com) states: 'Operating at the TMIB Anchorage in Brazil, Energos Nanook...Built by Samsung Heavy Industries, the vessel incorporates GTT Mark III membrane containment technology and direct open loop regasification systems...With recondenser-based boil-off gas management and Wärtsilä DFDE propulsion, Energos Nanook delivers reliable and efficient LNG import capacity.' DFDE = dual-fuel diesel-electric gensets producing the vessel's electric power. This is the vessel operator's own primary technical source (single primary/operator-technical source = green per SOP §confidence rules). No MW rating for the DFDE generator sets is disclosed publicly, so electric_mw is left blank per the 'documented existence without a figure is still YES' rule.

verification_log.note: confirms vessel capacity matches Sergipe FSRU

gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT neighbor Porto de Sergipe power station (3,509 MW aggregate/5 units, 3.68 km) is the separate onshore 1,500 MW combined-cycle plant the FSRU supplies regasified gas to, per the IDB Invest project financing page ('design, construction and operation of a 1500-MW combined cycle natural gas power plant...including an offshore regasification plant'). It is NOT the FSRU's captive power — it is the PowerPlantsSupplied relationship, already correctly recorded in GEM.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Onboard DFDE generation exists and is documented, but it is vessel-mounted FSRU auxiliary/propulsion power with no disclosed nameplate MW — matches the 'vessel-mounted, unclear GOGPT ontology fit' REVIEWER CALL criterion rather than ADD (no citable MW) or DO NOT ADD (generation is real, not absent).
status_or_other_findings: Ownership chain per gem.wiki-cited sources (not independently re-verified, not acted on): Golar Power/Hygo Energy Transition -> New Fortress Energy (2021) -> Eneva SA acquired 100% of Sergipe FSRU + Porto de Sergipe power station (Oct 2022) — consistent with GEM's current CELSE/Eneva owner/operator fields.
notes: Vessel 'Energos Nanook' was formerly 'Golar Nanook' before the Golar FSRU fleet's 2021 rebrand as Energos Infrastructure; both names are the same IMO 9785500 hull, confirmed by vessel-tracking cross-reference to Barra dos Coqueiros (the Sergipe terminal's anchorage).

No later disclosure of the vessel name or its technical specification was found in subsequent search.

verification_log.note: confirms vessel identity is contractually undisclosed as of May 2025

gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT neighbors Termopernambuco 2 (1,249 MW, cancelled, 1.05 km) and Termopernambuco (533 MW, operating, 1.28 km) are existing onshore gas-fired power stations at the Suape industrial complex — separate merchant/grid plants unrelated to this FSRU's own (undisclosed) equipment, not the terminal's captive power.
gogpt_candidate_basis: No FSRU vessel identity or generating equipment is public; nothing to add pending disclosure of the confidential charter.
notes: Worth a re-check in a future batch once the vessel identity is disclosed (contract was signed as confidential in May 2025; construction was ongoing per gem.wiki as of this run).

FEPAM's own environmental-licensing announcement confirms the two are licensed as distinct facilities (gas terminal + power plant); no source describes any onsite generation equipment for the terminal itself.

verification_log.note: confirms separate gas station + thermoelectric plant licensing, no onsite generation for the terminal itself

gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT neighbor Rio Grande power station (1,238 MW, announced, 2.07 km) is the very UTE this terminal was designed to feed, per the same FEPAM article — confirming the PowerPlantsSupplied direction, not a captive-power relationship.
